checks.label: An instrument calibrated for its range = 4 to 20 mA: the ideal line sends 4 mA at the bottom of the 0 to 10 bar range, 20 mA at the top and 12 mA half way, and the chain's display turns that back into 5.00 bar

The zero adjustment produces a parallel shift of the input-output line, and the span adjustment changes its slope: every zero setting moves all five check readings by the same amount and keeps the slope, and every span setting changes the slope and leaves the bottom end where it was

Span is the algebraic difference between the upper and lower range values: the relabelled range's typed span is its top minus its bottom, the same span as the first range, and its brace shows it only once checked

With a percentage of full-scale statement the error stays the same size throughout the range, and as a percentage of the reading it goes up as the reading goes down: the band is the same width in bar at every pressure, and the error as a share of the reading rises steadily as the reading falls

Accuracy is the closeness of agreement between a measured value and a true or accepted value: panel D's tight beads all sit well off the ideal line until the zero screw slides them down, and then they sit on it

Every worked figure is right: 6.25 bar sends 14 mA (slips 10 and 12.5); −1 to 9 bar spans 10 bar (slips 9 and 8); 0.32 mA high is 2% of span (slips 0.32, 8 and 1.6); a −0.48 mA span screw reads 7.88, 11.76, 15.64 and 19.52 mA, −0.75, −1.50, −2.25 and −3.00%; 20.40 mA at 10 bar is 2.5% there and 1.25% half way, 12.20 mA (slips 2.5, 0.2 and 0); ±0.5% of a 10 bar span is 5% of a 1 bar reading (slips 0.5, 0.05 and 50)

The table works each error from the rule and flags any above 0.5% of span: the span error screen fills 4.00, 7.88, 11.76, 15.64 and 19.52 mA at 0.00, −0.75, −1.50, −2.25 and −3.00%, the last four flagged, and a 0.32 mA zero error reads +2.00% at every point

The three other troubles: the down run reads 0.16 mA, 1% of span, high at 25, 50 and 75% and the same as the up run at the ends; every noise bead stays inside its band; a 0.1 bar display shows 6.3 bar for 6.26, 6.27 and 6.33 bar but not 6.24 or 6.36; a 0.5 bar display climbs in 20 steps over the range
Before a typed answer is checked its picture never shows it, and once checked it does: the 14.00 mA bead label, the 10 bar span, the +2.00% errors, the +1.25% half way row and the ±0.05 bar

A zero error and a span error can cancel in the middle: 4.16 mA at 0 bar and 19.84 mA at 10 bar read +1.00% and −1.00% at the ends and 0.00% half way; with the zero alone set right, 10 bar reads 19.68 mA, −2.00%; once answered both screws end at 0
Each typed answer is accepted with or without its unit, and each slip is refused with its own hint
